outline: Disorders of the stomach, small intestine, colon
Foundational lipid absorption and lipoprotein assembly
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTTP/MTP) transfers triglyceride and other neutral lipids to nascent apolipoprotein B within the endoplasmic reticulum. This step is required for assembly and secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins: chylomicrons from intestinal epithelial cells and VLDL from hepatocytes. Biallelic loss-of-function MTTP variants cause abetalipoproteinemia, with extremely low or absent apoB-containing lipoproteins, fat and fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption, acanthocytosis, and progressive neurologic/retinal complications if untreated.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy has chronic bulky greasy stools, poor weight gain, and progressive unsteadiness while walking. Examination shows diminished ankle reflexes. Peripheral blood smear shows numerous acanthocytes. Serum vitamin E is markedly reduced, and plasma apolipoprotein B is nearly undetectable. His LDL cholesterol and triglyceride concentrations are extremely low.
lead: Which of the following intracellular processes is most directly impaired in this patient?
correct: Transfer of triglyceride to nascent apolipoprotein B in the endoplasmic reticulum during assembly of chylomicrons and VLDL
distractors: Hydrolysis of triglycerides in circulating chylomicrons by lipoprotein lipase
Transport of prechylomicron particles from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi by SAR1B-dependent vesicles
Esterification of free cholesterol in plasma by lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase
Receptor-mediated uptake of LDL particles through the LDL receptor
distractor_notes: Lipoprotein lipase acts extracellularly on circulating triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. Deficiency causes marked hypertriglyceridemia and chylomicronemia rather than nearly absent apoB-containing lipoproteins.

SAR1B defects cause chylomicron retention disease by impairing prechylomicron transport from ER to Golgi. They primarily disrupt intestinal chylomicron secretion rather than the global MTTP-dependent assembly of both intestinal chylomicrons and hepatic VLDL.
LCAT esterifies cholesterol in plasma, especially during HDL maturation. LCAT deficiency does not prevent apoB-containing lipoprotein assembly in the ER.
LDL-receptor deficiency impairs LDL clearance and causes high LDL cholesterol rather than extremely low LDL and apoB.
key_expl: The findings indicate abetalipoproteinemia caused by MTTP deficiency. MTTP is located in the endoplasmic reticulum of enterocytes and hepatocytes and transfers neutral lipid to nascent apoB. Without this lipid-transfer step, apoB-containing lipoproteins cannot be assembled and secreted normally, producing a severe deficiency of chylomicrons, VLDL, and LDL. The resulting fat and fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption explains the low vitamin E, neurologic findings, and acanthocytosis.
objective: Connect abetalipoproteinemia to loss of MTTP-mediated lipid transfer onto nascent apoB in the endoplasmic reticulum, preventing formation of chylomicrons and VLDL and causing fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption.
clues: very low LDL cholesterol and triglycerides

sources.title: Current Diagnosis and Management of Abetalipoproteinemia
sources.support: The review states that MTTP resides in the ER of hepatocytes and intestinal epithelial cells, transfers triglyceride and cholesterol ester to apoB, and is essential for formation of VLDL and chylomicrons.
